messages:
alejandro: Heads up — spotted an oddity in the latency dashboard for eu-prod. p50 for /v1/generate is ~30ms higher in the console rollup but endpoint-level breakdowns don’t show it. Anyone seeing synthetic/load-test traffic leaking into rollups?

maria: Yup saw that earlier. p50 moved up, p99 basically flat. My hunch is the synthetic tag isn’t making it to the aggregator, so the rollup includes test traffic while the endpoint view (filtered at ingress) does not.

jamal: Do we still tag loadgen runs with source=synthetic? IIRC the load tool sets X-Test-Source header which our pipeline uses to set tag.

tess: We do when run from devbox: `./tools/load --tag synthetic`. But our k8s cron for the periodic canary uses a different container entrypoint and I don’t see the header being set there. Could be the canary path never sets the header.

alejandro: Quick repro query I ran in console to confirm:
```sql
SELECT p50, p95, p99 FROM latency_rollups
WHERE deployment='eu-prod' AND route='/v1/generate'
GROUP BY hour
```
If I add `AND tag!='synthetic'` the p50 drops back to expected baseline. Without the filter the median is skewed.

jamal: Ugh — so synthetic is being recorded without tag. Possibly envoy/proxy is stripping X-Test-Source on the canary runner. CC @oncall-jen for routing/proxy policy check.

oncall-jen: Looking. There was an envoy config tweak in the last deploy that standardized headers and dropped some non-whitelisted headers. Might have accidentally removed the test header. Will investigate and revert if needed.

deploy-bot: :warning: deploy 2026-03-23T07:50Z applied envoy-config-canary to eu-prod (id: cfg-98123)

oncall-jen: Reverted the header whitelist change as a hotfix to restore X-Test-Source. Rolling back now.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: revert-envoy-config applied to eu-prod (deploy 2026-03-23T08:15Z)

tess: If the revert fixes ingestion, we still need a console UX improvement — a simple toggle to exclude "internal/synthetic" from SLO charts and rollout cohorts. Product side should weigh in.

maria: Agreed. Also want a provenance badge on the latency tiles that shows sample counts and if known internal tags are present (so folks see when medians might be polluted).

jamal: Telemetry note: adding provenance metadata to rollups (e.g., counts split by known "source" tag) is doable but increases rollup cardinality and storage. We should discuss retention/storage tradeoffs.

alejandro: Short-term proposal: console query defaults to excluding known internal tags and shows a yellow warning: "Results include internal load tests — click to show" with a link to runbook. Long-term: pipeline should drop synthetic at aggregator ingestion or emit separate rollups.

tess: :thumbsup: I’ll write a short RFC for the UI toggle and the warning UX. For the short-term patch I can add the exclude-by-default filter to the SLO queries.

maria: Also need to reconcile dedicated vs hosted behavior — dedicated clusters may still use the older proxy path so they might keep recording the header correctly, which explains the divergence in some customers' dashboards.

jamal: I’ll open an infra ticket to add the header to the canary/k8s runner and verify all entrypoints set X-Test-Source. Assigning to infra-team.

alejandro: Leaving a small log bundle for the window I investigated (1782349000-1782349300) in case anyone needs it: https://redwood.internal/logs/abcd (internal-only).

oncall-jen: Monitoring update: p50 returned to baseline after revert. Rollup aggregation may lag by a few minutes — keep an eye on the console. If anyone sees reappearing skew, ping me and I’ll escalate.

-- end of thread --
